audit.whatIsWrong: content win[0] reads Skill while early says 'Level 1-2 Tryndamere bullies you' and whys[0] says he wins the first exchange outright. win[2] and win[3] read Tryndamere and Skill while whys[2] and whys[3] say level 3 flips the lane hard to Aatrox and 4-5 you out-brawl him. win[5] reads Tryndamere while whys[5] says first item widens YOUR lead.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Tryndamere, Tryndamere, Aatrox, Aatrox, Tryndamere, Aatrox, Tryndamere — which matches the prose exactly: he bullies levels 1-2, loses 3-5, takes Level 6 on Undying Rage, loses first item, wins late on crit scaling.
audit.corrected: Level 1 to Tryndamere; Levels 3 and 4-5 to Aatrox; Level 6 stays Tryndamere; First item to Aatrox; Two+ items stays Tryndamere.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] builds the first-item spike around 'Eclipse/Goredrinker'. Goredrinker has not been purchasable for several seasons and is not an item on 26.15.
audit.why: A named item a player cannot find in the shop destroys trust in everything else on the page. I removed the name rather than substituting one, because Aatrox's current first-item ordering is not verifiable from the local kit files and I will not invent it. Undying Rage's cooldown (120/100/80) was also missing from the Level 6 spike, which is the one number that decides when you re-commit.
audit.corrected: Goredrinker removed; 120s Undying Rage and its 5s duration stated with the re-engage timing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout is never mentioned anywhere in the entry, and it is the ability that decides whether you can leave a lost trade. It slows only enemies whose backs are turned to him, so running away from Tryndamere is what makes him fast enough to catch you.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Tryndamere lets out an insulting cry, decreasing surrounding champions' Attack Damage. Enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced.' Facing him while you back off takes the slow off entirely — and it also cuts your AD, which is why your damage feels wrong mid-trade. Neither half is in the entry. Spinning Slash is 12s at rank 1 and needs a target unit, so denying it a body is the other half of disengaging.
audit.corrected: Mocking Shout's back-turned condition and its AD reduction stated in spikes[0] and mid; Spinning Slash named as a targeted dash with its 12s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Bloodlust is described as 'low-cooldown crit heals' with no anti-heal answer named.
audit.why: Bloodlust is a 12s heal that consumes Fury and grows stronger the lower his health gets, so his sustain is at its best exactly when you have almost killed him. Grievous Wounds is what converts a won trade into a kill.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal named in the full-layer tldr alongside the 12s Bloodlust.

edits.before: With all three Q casts and E lifesteal online, walk him down: land the third-cast sweetspot knockup to interrupt his spin-to-you and chunk him past his low-fury heal.
edits.after: Walk him down with all three Q casts: the third-cast knockup interrupts Spinning Slash (12s). Never turn your back — Mocking Shout slows only those facing away.

edits.before: His level-6 Undying Rage (R) is the swing tool — bait it early, then kite the 5s and re-engage when it drops; don't commit into a full-fury Trynda or he'll crit through your drain.
edits.after: Undying Rage (120s) is the swing tool — bait it early, walk out the 5 seconds he cannot die, and re-engage on a Tryndamere with no ult. Never open into full Fury, or he crits through your drain.

edits.before: After Eclipse/Goredrinker you out-sustain and out-burst him in an extended trade — chain Q sweetspots and W pull to keep him from spinning to safety.
edits.after: On your first item you out-sustain and out-burst him in an extended trade — chain Q sweetspots and drag him back with W so his 12s Spinning Slash has no exit.

edits.before: Level 3 through 4-5 and your first item are Aatrox-favoured — Q sweetspot knockups interrupt his spin and let you drain through Bloodlust. The exception is level 6: once Undying Rage is up he wins the all-in, so bait it out or trade knowing you can't kill him for its 5 seconds, then re-commit at 7+ or on your first item. Track his E cooldown so he can't spin away after you land your combo.
edits.after: Level 3 through 4-5 and your first item are yours — sweetspot knockups interrupt Spinning Slash and you drain through the 12s Bloodlust. Level 6 is the exception: for the 5 seconds of Undying Rage he cannot die, so bait it, then re-commit on its 120s. Back away facing him: Mocking Shout only slows turned backs, and it saps your AD regardless. Track his 12s E so he cannot spin off.

edits.before: Spin (E) onto you for free damage then disengage before your Q lands
edits.after: Spin in on a target, then Mocking Shout your turned back as you leave

edits.before: Tryndamere changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Tryndamere Fury, Spin, and Undying Rage. Aatrox wins by controlling spacing with his first two Q swings, holding E until the enemy punish tool is committed, and managing the wave so the enemy must walk into the outer edge of his Q. Tryndamere wants to enter inside Aatrox clean Q hits on the outer edge (where it hurts most), force melee trades, and punish Aatrox after Q/E are down.
edits.after: Tryndamere changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect a 12s Bloodlust that heals hardest at low health, a targeted 12s Spinning Slash, and the 5 seconds of Undying Rage in which he simply cannot die. Aatrox wins by spacing with his first two Darkin Blade swings, backing off while facing him so Mocking Shout's slow never applies, and buying Grievous Wounds so a won trade turns into a kill rather than a reset.

edits.before: Tryndamere Fury, Spin, and Undying Rage
edits.after: Mocking Shout slows a turned back only

notes: Removed 'Goredrinker' from spikes[2] — the item does not exist on 26.15. I did not substitute a replacement because Aatrox's current first item is not verifiable from local files; the same stale name was flagged independently by the Tahm Kench mirror, so it likely recurs across champ-data/content/aatrox.js and deserves a file-wide itemisation pass. Battle Fury (his passive) is also never named in the entry — Fury drives both his crit chance and the size of the Bloodlust heal, so 'full-fury Trynda' is doing work the reader has no name for.
